newsitem.title: CHINA: Consumer spending in China capital steady.
newsitem.headline: Consumer spending in China capital steady.

text.p: Consumer spending in China's capital, Beijing, showed virtually no growth in the first quarter of this year, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

The percentage of consumer spending on food by the city's 11 million residents has continued to decrease while spending on electrical appliances continued to rise, it said, quoting the city's Statistics Bureau.
A Beijing family spent an average 1,497 yuan per capita on consumption in the first quarter, up by 6.8 percent compared with the year-ago period, but an actual rise of 0.4 percent after inflation.
Beijing residents' spending in eight major categories increased, except on clothes, it said.

Spending on medical care increased most, by 54 percent, on transportation and communication by 39 percent, on housing by 21 percent, on household facilities by 11 percent and miscellaneous items by nine percent, it said.
Spending on food rose by 3.3 percent and spending on entertainment and education was up by 0.5 percent.
